questions: Resilience architecture
D4
Cloud Pak for Integration
A CP4I platform team must define standard resilience tiers that application teams select from. Which approach is MOST effective?

Publish tiered reference patterns (for example Tier 1: multi-zone HA plus warm DR with tested failover and RPO near 0 in-region; Tier 2: multi-zone HA plus backup-based DR; Tier 3: single-zone with backups), each with defined RTO and RPO, cost, required CP4I configurations (Native HA, RF=3, n3 profiles, replicas) and testing obligations
Let each team design resilience from scratch
Apply the most expensive tier to every integration
Apply no resilience until an incident occurs
Standard tiers align investment with criticality, speed up design and make testing obligations explicit.
Correct: tiered, costed, testable reference patterns.
Wrong: inconsistent and slow.
Wrong: wasteful.
Wrong: reactive and risky.
Payments choose Tier 1; internal reporting chooses Tier 3, at a third of the cost.
Resilience tiers = a menu of tested, costed patterns.

T4
IBM MQ

After a Native HA failover, an application reconnects successfully but some messages it had put just before the failure are missing, while others appear twice. The application uses non-persistent messages outside syncpoint for speed. What explains this?

Non-persistent messages are not guaranteed to survive failover, and puts outside syncpoint plus client retries after reconnection can cause loss and duplication; use persistent messages within syncpoint and idempotent processing for data that matters
Native HA always loses messages
Uniform clusters duplicate messages
The DLQ was full
Native HA replicates persistent data. Non-persistent messages and non-transactional retry logic weaken delivery guarantees across failover.
Correct: delivery semantics chosen by the application.
Wrong: committed persistent data is preserved.
Wrong: unrelated.
Wrong: unrelated.
Switching critical flows to persistent and transactional messaging removed the anomalies.
HA protects persistent, committed messages. Design guarantees in the application too.
